rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent bent-and-cantilevered mass across all four views, with the curve remaining consistent in plan and section and without visible view-to-view collisions. It is not merely a box: the bend gives a single dominant gesture, and the carved void/cantilever creates a meaningful street response rather than a sealed frontage. The silhouette is stepped only in a restrained way, more like a continuous upper modulation than arbitrary tiering, so it stays compatible with the neighborhood-living brief. The program fit is plausible because the form can support active ground threshold plus a calm upper mass, and the section suggests a usable public edge/canopy logic rather than an arbitrary sculptural object. The main weakness is that the access-edge response is present but not emphatic enough; the mass would benefit from a clearer ground seam or notch aligned to the verified frontage.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Larger complex and more distributed than this compact street-building brief; avoid over-fragmenting the candidate into multiple wings.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise campus-like composition with terraced circulation and a legible central/public void; useful as a precedent for articulated neighborhood massing without becoming tower-like.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Simple rectilinear mass with a clear public edge condition and a restrained upper profile; useful for active-ground neighborhood uses.
